title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §5 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The aim is to describe pairs (ρ̃, σ̃) in a form PG of PGL(2) over a base scheme S whose product ε̃0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃ is regular unipotent. These are the images of the standard generators of PSL2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3: σ is the elliptic element of order 2, ρ the elliptic element of order 3, and ε0 the cusp loop. The relation ρσ^{-1}ε0 type is the 'loop equation' of M_{1,1}.

The page first finishes the normal-form statement begun on p.331. Under (41)/(44), there is a unique iso φ: GL(2)_S → G carrying ρ0 = [[0,1],[v,w]] and σ0 = [[0,-1],[-v,1-w]] (v a unit) to the canonical lifts ρ, σ. Then (48) gives
- (ε0)_0 = -σ0^{-1}ρ0 = [[1,1/v],[0,1]],
- (ε1)_0 = -ρ0σ0^{-1} = [[1,0],[1,1]].
Conversely, for any iso φ the images of ρ0, σ0 satisfy (41) and are lifts satisfying (44).

Check: det σ0 = -v and σ0^{-1} = (-1/v)[[1-w,1],[v,0]]. Hence σ0^{-1}ρ0 = [[-1,-1/v],[0,-1]] and -ρ0σ0^{-1} = [[1,0],[1,1]]. Both are correct. Also ρ0+σ0 = diag(0,1) is idempotent, matching (44) 2°.

The page then opens the 'Théorème d'épinglage modulaire' (modular pinning theorem). Let G, SG, PG be the forms of GL2, SL2, PGL2 attached to a rank-4 Azumaya algebra M over S. A 'modular triplet' in PG is (ρ̃, σ̃, ε̃0) with:
- (49) ε̃0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃, so that ε̃1 := ρ̃σ̃^{-1} = ρ̃(ε̃0) = σ̃(ε̃0) by conjugation;
- (50) ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 = 1 and ε̃0 regular unipotent (equivalently ε̃1 is);
- (51) ε̃0 and ε̃1 are fibrewise non-equivalent. Equivalently, for the unipotent lifts ε_i = 1+N_i in G, N0 and N1 are nowhere homothetic, i.e. they have distinct kernel lines in every fibre.
The page breaks off while defining a modular triplet in G.

Combined with p.331, the extra conditions pin down the parameters:
- σ̃^2 = 1 forces tr σ0 = 0, i.e. w = 1;
- ρ̃^3 = 1 forces tr^2 = det, i.e. w^2 = -v, so v = -1.
This yields the standard triplet ρ0 = [[0,1],[-1,1]], σ0 = [[0,-1],[1,0]], ε0 = [[1,-1],[0,1]] of the next page. So the theorem amounts to this: modular triplets in PG correspond bijectively and functorially in S to isomorphisms PGL(2)_S ≅ PG. The functor of modular triplets is a PG-torsor (equivalently an Aut-torsor) trivialised by a choice, i.e. a 'pinning' of the form by the image of the modular group.
errors: The form attached to M is written 'GPL(2)' on this page (and 'GP(1)' elsewhere); PGL(2) = PGL(1)-projective group is meant. This is a notational slip.

(51) as transcribed says 'équivalents/homologues' and 'homothétiques'. The intended (and correct) condition, consistent with p.331 and p.333 and with (48), is NON-equivalent and NON-homothetic in every fibre.

Over bases where 2 or 3 is not invertible, the passage from ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 = 1 to the trace conditions (w = 1, v = -1) needs care. For instance, in characteristic 3 an element of order 3 in PGL2 may be unipotent. The page does not discuss this; the next page's (56) states the conditions in lifted form (σ^2+1 = 0, ρ^2-ρ+1 = 0), which avoids the issue.
In (49) the 'i.e.' form ρ̃^{-1}σ̃ε̃0 = 1 is correct in PG. In G the sign matters (cf. (52): ρ^{-1}σε0 = -1). This is a consistent but easily confused sign convention.

ideas.what: Normal form of a pair (ρ, σ) in a form of GL2 with σ^{-1}ρ regular unipotent and ε0, ε1 fibrewise non-equivalent. It yields a unique isomorphism with GL2 carrying the pair to [[0,1],[v,w]], [[0,-1],[-v,1-w]], with explicit ε0 = [[1,1/v],[0,1]] and ε1 = [[1,0],[1,1]].
ideas.modern_name: Trivialisation of forms of GL2/PGL2 via a pair of opposite regular unipotents (a pinning / épinglage)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pinnings of reductive group schemes: Demazure–Grothendieck (SGA 3)
ideas.where_published: General épinglage theory is in SGA 3 (Exp. XXIII–XXIV). This specific explicit normal form is not known to me in print.

ideas.what: 'Modular pinning theorem': triplets (ρ̃, σ̃, ε̃0) in PG with ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 = 1, ε̃0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃ regular unipotent, and ε̃0, ε̃1 non-equivalent fibrewise. These correspond bijectively to isomorphisms PGL2_S ≅ PG sending the standard PSL2(Z) generators to the triplet.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / scheme-theoretic moduli of the standard representation of PSL2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 into forms of PGL2; pinning of an Azumaya quaternion form by modular-group data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (presentation of PSL2(Z) by elliptic generators; rigidity folklore); no specific attribution known
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know (unsure).

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the modular group's standard triple (order 2, order 3, cusp) as a pinning datum for arbitrary forms of PGL2 over any base. This is presumably meant to make the modular tower / loop equation work integrally over arbitrary S and twisted forms (Azumaya algebras). It is a small, clean, but essentially elementary statement; I do not know it in this form in print.
missed.quote: Théorème d'épinglage modulaire Soient G, SG, PG des formes ... associées à une alg. d'Azumaya M de rg. 4. ... Appelons triplet modulaire dans PG ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a base-free description of the 'modular' structure underlying actions on M_{1,1} and the PSL2(Z) part of Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, compatible with twisted forms (quaternion algebras). Its interest is mainly as context for the loop-equation work rather than as a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are correct and elementary (normal form of a pinned pair in GL2). The 'modular pinning' formulation over arbitrary S for Azumaya forms is a tidy unpublished framing, but would not surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: (51) should read roughly 'ε̃0 et ε̃1 sont non équivalents fibre par fibre' (insertion above, perhaps 'inéquivalents'), and later 'que N0 et N1 sont non homothétiques en toute fibre', not 'équivalents/homologues' and 'homothétiques'.
In (48), the deleted item before the second matrix is a struck-out '(ε1)0'. Its definition (ε1)0 = -ρ0σ0^{-1} is written above, so the second matrix [[1,0],[1,1]] is (ε1)0.
Title: 'Théorème d'épinglage modulaire' (the previous page's 'épi-glogage' is the same word, épinglage).
'GPL(2)' as written by Grothendieck stands for PGL(2) (elsewhere GP(1)).
